output.population: 215 overweight people with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, never treated with antihyperglycemic drugs, HbA1c <11%, at a teaching hospital in Naples, Italy.
output.intervention: Low-carbohydrate Mediterranean-style diet (<50% of daily calories from carbohydrates), n=108.
output.intervention_or_exposure: Low-carbohydrate Mediterranean-style diet (<50% of daily calories from carbohydrates).
output.comparator: Low-fat diet (<30% of daily calories from fat), n=107.
output.outcome: Initiation of antihyperglycemic drug therapy when follow-up HbA1c was >7% (primary outcome); secondary outcomes included weight, glycemic control, and coronary risk factors.
output.effect: After 4 years, 44% in the Mediterranean-style group versus 70% in the low-fat group required drug therapy; absolute difference -26.0 percentage points (95% CI -31.1 to -20.1); hazard ratio 0.63 (CI 0.51 to 0.86); weight-change-adjusted hazard ratio 0.70 (CI 0.59 to 0.90); P<0.001.
output.applicability_boundary: Applies to overweight, drug-naive patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and HbA1c <11% in this single-center trial; drug-initiation investigators were unblinded and dietary intake was self-reported.
output.source_span: After 4 years, 44% of patients in the Mediterranean-style diet group and 70% in the low-fat diet group required treatment.

uncertainties: Investigators responsible for initiating drug therapy were not blinded to treatment assignment.
